title: Handoff Security Contracts and Audit Notes
content:
Context and purpose:
This is an informal product draft capturing proposed language and operational wiring for customer-managed networking handoffs, the required security contracts we ask for at onboarding, and the audit log semantics we need from the customer side. The goal is to land a small set of prescriptive requirements we can include in the Private Deployment onboarding checklist (operator runbook) and to clarify which signals the Control Plane needs for post-handoff monitoring and audits.

Why this matters: quick summary
- Private deployments are high-touch: customers expect the handoff to be low-risk and auditable.
- Many support incidents come from ambiguous ownership after we hand over networking, peering, or firewall rules.
- We need a minimal, machine-checkable set of artifacts from customer operator teams so we can close SLA/attestation loops without requiring months of custom compliance work.

Primary objectives (what this doc tries to do)
1) Define a machine-readable "Handoff Contract" that the customer signs off on during onboarding: expected firewall rules, peering endpoints, cert rotation responsibilities, and minimum audit log retention.
2) Define a set of mandatory audit events (and preferred formats) that the customer must export to our secure ingest or provide via an agreed query interface.
3) Define approval gates during the handoff flow where Redwood must assert certain telemetry is present before we mark the deployment as "externally-managed" and reduce our active controls.
4) Provide operator-facing runbook text for the onboarding SRE/solutions engineer to follow.

Non-goals
- This doc is not a finished legal contract. It informs engineering and pre-sales what types of artifacts to collect. Legal will convert into specific phrasing later.
- We're not solving every NIST/SOC control out of the box. Aim for pragmatic coverage to reduce the most common operational failures.

Target personas
- Customer infra/operator (primary): needs a concise checklist they can run in <2 hours.
- Redwood solutions engineer / onboarding SRE (secondary): uses the runbook to validate the handoff.
- Product/security reviewer (tertiary): wants explicit signals to include in customer SLAs and attestation docs.

Core proposal: Handoff Contract (machine-friendly JSON spec)
- Name: handoff_contract_v1 (example schema outline below shown as human readable list; engineering will define exact JSON schema in a follow-up PR)
- Required entries:
  - customer_vpc_id: canonical id we use in our tickets
  - accepted_peers: list of IP/CIDR endpoints allowed for Redwood control-plane and data-plane connections
  - admin_contact: email/phone for emergency escalation
  - audit_export_endpoint: URL or s3-like uri where customer will push logs (signed read-only role details attached)
  - audit_types: ["connection_attempt", "security_group_change", "route_change", "peering_config_change", "kex_failure"]
  - retention_days: minimum number of days logs retained (default 90)
  - rotation_policy_ack: boolean indicating customer accepts cert/key rotation cadence (default 30/90 days depending on cert type)
  - fallback_approval_policy: small enum {redwood-rollback, customer-rollback, joint-rollback}

Mandatory audit events (minimum set we require)
- connection_attempt: all TCP/TLS connect attempts involving Redwood IP ranges, timestamped, with src/dst, outcome
- security_group_change: record of any change to SG/NACL rules that could open inbound ranges to Redwood endpoints
- route_change: BGP/route-table modifications that affect packet flow to the data plane
- peering_config_change: events for establishing/tearing peering relationships incl. ASN and ACLs applied
- admin_approval: any change that was gated by customer admin (who approved, ticket ref)

Format guidance (preference order)
1) Structured JSON lines (ndjson) with schema registry reference (preferred)
2) CEF/CEF-like if customer SIEM uses it (acceptable)
3) Raw syslog (acceptable if enriched and with stable timestamps)

Approval gates (where Redwood blocks final handoff)
- Gate 1: Network path validation (automated)
  - Redwood runs basic connectivity tests from control-plane to data-plane endpoints. Fail -> do not mark as externally-managed.
- Gate 2: Audit export reachable and sampleable (manual + automated)
  - Validate the audit_export_endpoint is reachable, accepts auth, and returns at least 7 days of recent events (or a sample). If logs missing, raise to customer and hold.
- Gate 3: Admin contact verified + on-call test
  - Call or Slack-based verification to confirm emergency contact and rotation owner.
- Gate 4 (optional): Net changes gating window set by customer
  - During first 30 days post-handoff, require that any network/peering change has a joint approval ticket and is scheduled in a maintenance window.

Operational runbook (for onboarding SE/SRE)
- Step 0: Create onboarding ticket in JIRA and attach handoff_contract_v1 checklist.
- Step 1: Get customer to fill contract and share audit_export_role/credentials (least-privilege).
- Step 2: Run network path validation script (link to script in linked_artifacts). Capture output and attach to ticket.
- Step 3: Validate logs: pull 7-day sample via provided endpoint. Run parser to check for required event types. Document any missing types as "blockers".
- Step 4: Execute admin contact verification call (scripted questions in appendix).
- Step 5: If all gates pass, mark ticket state = ready-for-production; change internal flag and schedule 30-day soft-lock.

Acceptance criteria (how we know this works)
- 80% of new private deployments complete handoff within 48 hours using this flow (baseline today is ~6 days)
- Onboarding tickets that pass all gates have <10% post-handoff networking incidents in first 90 days
- Automated checks detect missing audit events in >=95% of misconfigured environments (once parser matured)

Edge cases and open questions
- Q1: Customers with strict SIEM policies refuse to expose an endpoint; can we accept periodic signed snapshots pushed by customer? (proposed: yes, but need signed timestamping and replay protection)
- Q2: Air-gapped/on-prem sites — how do we get log samples? (proposed: collection agent guidelines + manual handshake process in runbook)
- Q3: How strict is retention_days for regulated customers? Is 90 days enough? (ask legal/compliance for different regions)
- Q4: Who owns alerting for network anomalies after handoff? (propose: customer primary; Redwood optional co-monitoring for premium SLA)

Appendix: Suggested fields for onboarding ticket description (copy/paste template)
- Customer name:
- VPC IDs:
- Proposed peering endpoints:
- Audit export URI (and role):
- Admin on-call contact (name/email/phone):
- Expected go-live date:
- Gate statuses (network, audit, admin verified):

Next steps (short-term)
- Product: finalize JSON schema and publish registry item (owner: Marco) — due 2024-09-18.
- Eng: implement log validator script and integrate into onboarding automation (owner: Priya) — prototype by 2024-10-02.
- Solutions/SE: trial this with 2 upcoming customers this quarter and capture time-to-complete metrics (owner: Eliot).
- Compliance/Legal: draft candidate contract language to be reviewed by security — request by 2024-09-25.

Notes and references
- See linked_artifacts for current runtime PR that touches peering checks.
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-onsite (search for "handoff contract" for prior discussion)
